data.long_meaning: Derived from the Old Irish name Colleen meaning 'hazel-eyed'. This name was popularized in Ireland during the 19th century and has since become a common name for Irish girls. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Greek, Latin. Parents who choose Coleen usually hope their child will grow to embody hazel-eyed and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.cultural_impact: The name Colleen gained popularity through the works of Irish poet W.B. Yeats and his play "TheCountess Cathleen", which featured a generous and kind-hearted character named Colleen Bawn. The play showcased Irish folklore, mythology, and themes of redemption and transformation, leaving a lasting impact on Irish culture and literature.
data.spiritual_significance: In Irish mythology, the hazel tree was considered sacred due to its nut producing power, which represented renewal and rebirth. Colleen, meaning 'hazel-eyed', carries this symbolism in her name. Additionally, spiritual significant is attached to the name through its association with the Irish saints Colman and Columcille, both of whom had significant roles in Irish monasticism and scholarship. The name Coleen is believed to bestow the bearer with the virtues of kindness, generosity, and wisdom.
